desc:
You are given a lowercase string s and an array shifts of the same length. Process i = 0, 1, ..., n - 1 in order: the i-th step shifts each of the first i + 1 letters forward through the alphabet by shifts[i] places, wrapping from z to a.

Return the string after all steps.

s = "xyz", shifts = [1, 2, 4]
result = "eed"

The first letter is shifted by 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 (x → e), the second by 2 + 4 = 6 (y → e) and the third by 4 (z → d).
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Applying every step to a whole prefix costs O(n) per step. Consider one single letter: which steps touch it?
Letter j is inside the prefix of every step i ≥ j, so its total shift is shifts[j] + shifts[j+1] + ... + shifts[n-1].
These are suffix sums. Walk from the right end keeping a running total (reduced modulo 26) and shift each letter by that total.
editorial: Shifts commute and only their sum matters for each letter. Letter j belongs to the first i + 1 letters exactly when i ≥ j, so it receives the sum of shifts[j..n-1].

Compute the suffix sums from right to left in one pass. Because the alphabet has 26 letters, keep the running sum modulo 26 (the true sum can reach 5 × 1012, which would overflow 32-bit integers in some languages). Then letter j becomes (letter + total) mod 26. Time O(n), space O(n).
